items.title: Faithfulness Without Anchors: A Position Paper on the Structural Misalignments of Explainable AI Faithfulness Metrics for Feature Importance
items.description:
arXiv:2610.12493v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) tools have often been presented as methods to increase trust in machine learning models by making aspects of their algorithms more human-understandable. However, evidence accumulated over the last decade points to an overall failure of this objective, instead promoting overreliance on incorrect predictions, which can subsequently lead to algorithmic aversion. Rather, XAI appears to function primarily as a debugging tool, useful for obtaining anecdotal insights into, for example, features learned by the model. One of the main issues underlying this limitation is that XAI methods often oversimplify the inner workings of the model, resulting in misalignment between the explanation and the model itself - a behavior referred to as unfaithfulness or infidelity. Faithfulness can be interpreted as the degree of approximation between an explanation and the model. Computing faithfulness in a rigorous manner would thus make it possible to quantify one of the various elements of trustworthiness of an explanation. However, existing metrics present significant limitations, making this quantification either infeasible or computationally expensive. In this position paper, we outline five major shortcomings of current faithfulness metrics and propose four possible avenues for research to bolster their reliability.

_analysis.title: 无锚点的忠实性：关于可解释AI忠实性度量结构性错位的立场论文
_analysis.summary: 本文指出XAI工具未能提升信任，反而导致过度依赖错误预测。作者分析了现有特征重要性忠实性度量的五大缺陷，并提出四个研究方向以提升其可靠性。

items.title: EliteTable: Self-Improving Program Search for Executable Control Policies
items.description:
arXiv:2610.12536v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: EliteTable is a self-improving program-search algorithm guided by large language models (LLMs) that uses a fixed-capacity table of high-scoring solutions to guide new proposals, edits of existing solutions, and remixes of several solutions. Performance was evaluated across six Gymnasium control tasks, each with ten generations and fifty candidate slots per generation. Each task was evaluated across ten independently initialized searches. Candidate-score medians rose between the first and final generations in all six tasks, and selected-winner search-score medians rose in five. In CartPole-v1, the selected winner reached the search-score ceiling in the first generation of all ten searches. All ten paired held-out endpoints improved in four of the six tasks. BipedalWalker-v3 and CarRacing-v3 improved without reaching their reporting targets. Six of ten Acrobot-v1 searches declined on held-out episodes, and the median paired change was negative. The results document improvement during program search and the transfer of selected-winner gains to new episodes in some tasks. Comparisons and ablations are needed to establish EliteTable's relative performance and the contributions of its components.

_analysis.title: EliteTable：面向可执行控制策略的自改进程序搜索
_analysis.summary: EliteTable 是一种由大语言模型引导的自改进程序搜索算法，使用固定容量的高分方案表来指导新提案、编辑和重组。在六个 Gymnasium 控制任务上评估，多数任务中候选分数中位数随代数提升，部分任务中获胜方案的增益可迁移到新回合。
_analysis.summary_en: EliteTable is a self-improving program-search algorithm guided by LLMs that uses a fixed-capacity table of high-scoring solutions to guide new proposals, edits, and remixes. Evaluated on six Gymnasium control tasks, candidate-score medians rose across generations in all six, and selected-winner gains transferred to held-out episodes in some tasks.

items.title: Equal-Budget Monte Carlo Tree Search versus Randomized-Restart List Scheduling for DAG Workflows: A Controlled Equal-Budget Computational Study
items.description:
arXiv:2610.12542v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) is often proposed for scheduling directed-acyclic-graph (DAG) workflows, yet most studies never run the comparison that could refute it - giving a much simpler method the same search effort. We run that comparison under a controlled protocol. All arms receive an identical budget - the same number of candidate schedules built and evaluated: an MCTS scheduling method, preregistered as the main arm; a randomized-restart list scheduler with no search tree as the control; and a textbook-UCT MCTS arm as a registered follow-up on the same domain. The analysis plan was locked before data collection; an independent checker confirmed all 768 confirmation-stage schedules valid with correct finish times. At the main budget of 2048 evaluated schedules, MCTS is 2.88% worse than the restarts (95% CI [-3.62%,-2.15%]; the 72 of 96 held-out instances with positive baseline-relative headroom). The deficit is not budget starvation: on the separate exploration pool restarts self-improve by 1.85% where MCTS gains 0.24%, and 700 of 720 of MCTS's first results are merely the warm start it was handed. The studied selection rule locks deterministically onto the first-expanded child, keeping its trials correlated while restarts draw gains from the tails; the causal link to makespan remains an inference. A structural map locates where the tree stops paying: restarts win on sparse irregular workflows, no difference is detectable on regular layered ones, and dense ones leave no room to improve. Swapping the rule for textbook UCT removes most of the deficit (-0.26%, 95% CI [-0.71%,+0.23%]) without reversing its sign. Results are confined to a controlled synthetic domain (N in {8,16,32} tasks, 2-8 processors, budgets up to 2048); we make no claim about larger budgets.

_analysis.title: 等预算下MCTS与随机重启列表调度在DAG工作流中的对比研究
_analysis.summary: 该研究在等预算条件下对比MCTS与随机重启列表调度在DAG工作流调度中的表现。结果显示，在2048次评估预算下，MCTS比随机重启差2.88%，且差距并非预算不足所致。随机重启在稀疏不规则工作流上优势明显，而MCTS的确定性选择规则导致试验相关性过高。
_analysis.summary_en: This study compares MCTS and randomized-restart list scheduling for DAG workflows under equal budgets. At 2048 evaluated schedules, MCTS is 2.88% worse than restarts, not due to budget starvation. Restarts excel on sparse irregular workflows, while MCTS's deterministic selection rule causes correlated trials.

items.title: Know What You Don't Know: Agentic Data Synthesis by Evolving Generation Space for Closed-Loop Learning
items.description:
arXiv:2610.12593v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The continued improvement of large language models increasingly depends on synthetic experience, yet effective data synthesis for interactive agents requires not only executable and verifiable trajectories, but also interactions that provide learning value for the current task agent. Existing methods increasingly incorporate environment feedback, data validation, or learner failures, but still face a feedback-to-decision gap: observed weaknesses do not directly specify how future synthesis should change, or whether they can be represented by the current synthesis space. To address this gap, we propose EvoSyn, a learning-feedback-driven multi-agent framework that organizes synthesis around a revisable state specifying what interaction factors can be deliberately generated and where synthesis effort should be allocated. A role-specialized multi-agent system translates learner feedback into synthesis revisions, while a Designer allocates synthesis directions and a Planner grounds them into executable experience. This process enables within-space adaptation toward weak or under-covered regions and synthesis-space expansion that promotes newly discovered factors into explicit generation controls. Experiments on $\tau^2$-Bench and CAR-Bench show that EvoSyn improves average task success by 13.3 points over the strongest synthesis baseline, while producing higher-quality and structurally broader synthetic experience and discovering controllable factors missed without learner feedback.

_analysis.title: EvoSyn：基于学习反馈的多智能体数据合成框架
_analysis.summary: 提出EvoSyn，一种学习反馈驱动的多智能体数据合成框架，通过可修订状态组织合成过程，将学习者反馈转化为合成修订，实现合成空间的适应与扩展。在τ²-Bench和CAR-Bench上平均任务成功率提升13.3个百分点，并生成更高质量、结构更广的合成经验。
_analysis.summary_en: Proposes EvoSyn, a learning-feedback-driven multi-agent framework for data synthesis that organizes synthesis around a revisable state, translating learner feedback into synthesis revisions to enable within-space adaptation and synthesis-space expansion. On τ²-Bench and CAR-Bench, it improves average task success by 13.3 points over the strongest baseline, producing higher-quality and structurally broader synthetic experience.

items.title: SpireBench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Strategic Play of Agentic Models with Slay the Spire
items.description:
arXiv:2610.12596v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agentic large language models now tackle complex tasks, yet strategic reasoning over long horizons is under-studied: most agentic benchmarks are short and episodic, and performance on long tasks is hard to dissect into stored knowledge, reasoning and luck. We introduce SpireBench, in which models play the complete commercial deck-builder Slay the Spire (StS), where early decisions decide long-term success. Across 20 large language models (LLMs) at the game's highest difficulty, frontier models beat heuristic baselines and match the average human player but remain far behind experts. This gap widens as the run lengthens: the strongest models win the first act as often as experts, then fall behind. What separates strong models from weak is how well they play each fight; all of them misjudge risk over a run, preserving health rather than spending it to grow stronger. A comprehensive, self-consistent renaming of every game term shows that part of their performance rests on prior knowledge of the game, and models do not improve from the memories they write across runs, which are often wrong and overly cautious. Our harness is the first to give a model the complete original game, and we compare it with existing harnesses. Overall, SpireBench offers an unsaturated long-horizon benchmark with tools to locate where and why agents fail.

_analysis.title: SpireBench：用《杀戮尖塔》评估智能体模型的长时程策略博弈
_analysis.summary: SpireBench 让 20 个大语言模型在最高难度下完整游玩商业卡牌构筑游戏《杀戮尖塔》，评估其长时程策略推理能力。前沿模型超越启发式基线并达到人类平均水平，但远逊于专家，且随游戏进程拉长差距扩大。模型普遍误判风险、过度保守，且无法从跨局记忆中改进。该基准可定位智能体失败的位置与原因。
_analysis.summary_en: SpireBench evaluates 20 LLMs playing the full commercial deck-builder Slay the Spire at highest difficulty. Frontier models beat heuristic baselines and match average humans but lag far behind experts, with the gap widening as runs lengthen. Models misjudge risk, play overly cautiously, and fail to improve from cross-run memories. It offers an unsaturated long-horizon benchmark to locate where and why agents fail.

items.title: AutoIndexer: Flexible-Order Decoding by Training Causal Models on Chains of Edits
items.description:
arXiv:2610.12545v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autoregressive decoding is less suited to non-causally ordered data, e.g., cross-references or future dependencies, since their outputs cannot be revised post hoc, unlike iterative human reasoning. Diffusion LLMs partially mitigate this limitation but still cannot flexibly insert or remove arbitrary numbers of tokens from a pre-generated context. We design AutoIndexer as a generative model with a novel training and decoding mechanism that simulates a Chain of Edits, allowing the model to flexibly modify its prior outputs in hindsight via token insertions, substitutions, and deletions. The model learns to predict marker tokens for opening and closing edits, simultaneously moving a cursor to positions in the existing token sequence, analogous to a text editor. Training sequences are obtained by perturbing ground-truth labels with inverse chained edit operations, and the model learns to edit by undoing those inverses. The perturbation training allows AutoIndexer to be robust to erroneous context and adaptable to editing tasks such as code correction. We demonstrate that our method exhibits post-generation context-editing capabilities that most autoregressive and diffusion models lack without compromising performance on standard LLM benchmarks. The code is available at https://github.com/AutodeskAILab/autoindexer.

_analysis.title: AutoIndexer：通过编辑链训练因果模型的灵活顺序解码
_analysis.summary: AutoIndexer 提出一种新的训练与解码机制，模拟“编辑链”，让模型能通过插入、替换、删除标记灵活修改已生成的输出，类似文本编辑器移动光标。训练序列由真实标签经逆向链式编辑扰动生成，模型学习撤销这些逆操作。该方法具备自回归和扩散模型缺乏的生成后上下文编辑能力，且不损失标准基准性能。
_analysis.summary_en: AutoIndexer introduces a novel training and decoding mechanism simulating a Chain of Edits, letting models flexibly modify prior outputs via token insertions, substitutions, and deletions like a text editor cursor. Training sequences are built by perturbing ground-truth labels with inverse chained edits, and the model learns to undo them. It enables post-generation context editing that autoregressive and diffusion models lack, without hurting standard benchmark performance.

items.title: SWE-Duel: Towards a Self-Scaling Arena for Coding Agents
items.description:
arXiv:2610.12569v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Static coding benchmarks are fixed at release. Over time their tasks leak into training data, and stronger agents eventually saturate them. We argue that a benchmark should instead aim to be self-scaling: its tasks and oracles are created at evaluation time, so no content exists in advance to leak, and its difficulty is set by the participating agents rather than fixed at release. We introduce SWE-Duel, an arena in which two coding agents evaluate each other over mirrored Red-Blue turns. In each turn, the Red agent works on a real repository across three context-isolated sessions. It proposes and implements a new feature with feature tests, then embeds a subtle bug in that feature along with sealed bug-triggering tests. The resulting pull request is admitted only if (1) it passes the feature tests and the repository's existing tests while failing exactly the bug tests, and (2) a fresh session of the same agent can repair the bug blind, which rules out unsolvable tasks. The Blue agent then reviews the pull request without being told a bug exists. It wins only if its revision passes all three test suites, and then the two agents swap roles. We run a tournament among 11 model-harness participants on 15 repositories in five languages for 1,500 turns. The leaders win in different ways. GPT-5.5 with Codex CLI ranks first as the strongest solver, repairing 98.3% of the defects it reviews. Claude Opus 4.8 with mini-swe-agent ranks second as the strongest task author, with a 27.3% Red win rate. Finally, within one model family, tasks written by the newest version defeat a fixed-reference solver far more often than those of older versions (42.9% vs. 4.0%), giving preliminary evidence that task difficulty scales with task authoring capability.

_analysis.title: SWE-Duel：面向编码智能体的自扩展竞技场
_analysis.summary: 提出SWE-Duel自扩展基准，任务与判定在评测时生成，避免数据泄漏与饱和。红蓝双方智能体在真实仓库上互评：红方实现新功能并植入隐蔽bug，蓝方盲审修复。11个模型在15个仓库、5种语言进行1500轮锦标赛，GPT-5.5修复98.3%缺陷，Claude Opus 4.8红方胜率27.3%，并发现任务难度随作者能力提升而扩展。
_analysis.summary_en: SWE-Duel introduces a self-scaling coding benchmark where tasks and oracles are generated at evaluation time, preventing leakage and saturation. Two agents duel over mirrored Red-Blue turns on real repositories: Red implements a feature with a hidden bug, Blue reviews blind. In a 1,500-turn tournament across 11 model-harness participants and 15 repos in 5 languages, GPT-5.5 repaired 98.3% of defects and Claude Opus 4.8 achieved a 27.3% Red win rate, with evidence that task difficulty scales with authoring capability.

items.title: Contextual Correction of Parallel Draftsfor Speculative Decoding
items.description:
arXiv:2610.12570v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model inference by using a lightweight drafter to propose multiple tokens that are subsequently verified in parallel by the target model. Recent diffusion-based drafters make this paradigm particularly attractive: deep attention-based neural backbones provide strong predictions, while drafting multiple future positions in parallel avoids the sequential cost of autoregressive generation. This parallelism, however, comes at a cost. Tokens within a draft block are predicted without access to the realized identities of preceding draft tokens, removing intra-block dependencies that would naturally be available under autoregressive generation. We introduce DCOCO (DFlash Contextual Corrector), a lightweight mechanism that restores these dependencies while preserving parallel drafting. Rather than committing to each position's top prediction, DCOCO retains multiple candidate tokens and evaluates their contextual compatibility across adjacent draft positions in parallel, enabling contextually informed token selection at low additional cost. Across four verifier backbones and ten benchmarks, DCOCO achieves the highest average throughput in every evaluated configuration, spanning greedy and stochastic decoding with and without extended reasoning, with speedups of up to 6.6x over vanilla decoding. Its advantage persists under concurrent serving: DCOCO outperforms the strongest competing method by 6-23% across 4-32 concurrent requests, while other sequential correctors fall below uncorrected DFlash at these loads. These results demonstrate that recovering intra-block dependencies through parallel contextual scoring delivers consistent acceleration across decoding regimes and serving loads.

_analysis.title: 并行草稿的上下文校正用于投机解码
_analysis.summary: 提出DCOCO机制，通过保留多个候选token并并行评估相邻草稿位置的上下文兼容性，恢复并行草稿中缺失的块内依赖关系。在四种验证器骨干和十个基准上实现最高平均吞吐量，相比普通解码最高加速6.6倍，并发服务下优于最强竞争方法6-23%。

Achieves highest average throughput across four verifier backbones and ten benchmarks, with up to 6.6x speedup over vanilla decoding and 6-23% improvement over the strongest competing method under concurrent serving.

items.title: CLUE: A Contrastive Learning Framework for Unsupervised Event Type Induction and Annotation
items.description:
arXiv:2610.12580v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Event ontology is the foundational framework for defining events in a dataset. Event type induction generally involves domain experts who define guidelines for creating event types and their names based on the dataset's domain and scope. However, this process is resource-intensive in terms of annotation costs and is prone to human biases. To alleviate the need for manual event ontology creation, we propose the CLUE framework for event type induction, naming, and annotation. Our main contributions in this work are: 1) designing a novel joint embedding representation for expressing both the verb-centric view and the semantic view of events; 2) event type induction using contrastive loss guided clustering; 3) event naming and refinement. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at https://github.com/PratikMaitra/CLUE.

_analysis.title: CLUE：无监督事件类型归纳与标注的对比学习框架
_analysis.summary: 提出CLUE框架，用于无监督事件类型归纳、命名与标注。主要贡献包括：设计联合嵌入表示同时表达动词中心视角与语义视角；利用对比损失引导聚类进行事件类型归纳；实现事件命名与优化。实验验证了方法有效性，代码已开源。
_analysis.summary_en: The CLUE framework is proposed for unsupervised event type induction, naming, and annotation. Key contributions include a novel joint embedding representation capturing both verb-centric and semantic views of events, contrastive loss guided clustering for event type induction, and event naming and refinement. Experiments demonstrate effectiveness, with code open-sourced.

_article.title: CLUE：无监督事件类型归纳与标注的对比学习框架
_article.summary: 提出CLUE框架，用于无监督事件类型归纳、命名与标注。主要贡献包括：设计联合嵌入表示同时表达动词中心视角与语义视角；利用对比损失引导聚类进行事件类型归纳；实现事件命名与优化。实验验证了方法有效性，代码已开源。
_article.summary_en: The CLUE framework is proposed for unsupervised event type induction, naming, and annotation. Key contributions include a novel joint embedding representation capturing both verb-centric and semantic views of events, contrastive loss guided clustering for event type induction, and event naming and refinement. Experiments demonstrate effectiveness, with code open-sourced.

items.title: One Model to Loop Them All: Elastic Latent Recurrence for Language Models
items.description:
arXiv:2610.12582v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A latent recurrent language model applies a shared block of layers repeatedly, so one checkpoint can trade inference compute for accuracy by changing the loop count. At one loop, however, such models typically fall well short of a non-recurrent model of the same size, a one-loop tax that makes a separate non-recurrent model the better choice whenever latency matters. We present Elastic Latent Recurrence (ELR), a recipe for training looped language models without this tax. At one loop, an ELR model costs the same to serve as a non-recurrent model of the same size and, trained on the same data, reaches similar accuracy. Each additional loop then buys more accuracy for more inference compute. Three choices make this work: a gated state update with a learned step size, loop counts mixed within each optimizer update, and conditioning each pass on its loop index and budget. The first two preserve one-loop accuracy, and the third lowers loss at every additional loop. Mixed depths can be introduced late in pretraining to limit the added training cost, and with zero-initialized conditioning added at the switch, this late schedule reaches lower loss than mixed-depth training from scratch. In MoE models, reusing first-loop expert routes on later loops cuts mixed-depth update time by 11.7% with no measurable change in accuracy. At inference, keeping only the last loop's attention KV cache holds attention KV memory at its one-loop level while retaining most of the gain from additional loops. On 4B dense and 30B-A3B MoE hybrid models, ELR at one loop is 0.52 points below and 1.04 points above its matched baseline on a ten-task average, and four loops add 7.25 and 4.75 points. Carried through post-training, the recipe yields Koi-4B, a single checkpoint that scores an estimated 18 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at one loop, matching Qwen3.5-4B, and 29 at four loops.
